title: Odile and the Compass
premise: Petra Galloway, a railroad engineer who has spent fifteen years mapping closed lines to stay off every official record, is hired quietly to investigate a vanished government survey team in the flooded river country. With only their abandoned gear and no tracks, he teams up with Odile, a boat pilot who knows the monsoon waters better than any chart, and discovers the team was erased because they found something the state wants buried: an old compass that points not north, but toward people. Hunted by the survey's sponsors, Petra must choose between disappearing again and claiming the belonging he never let himself want; the story ends with him burning his map of closed lines and staying through the flood season with Odile's crew, the compass surrendered to the river.
about_author: Emrys Marchetti is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent a decade charting seasonal waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who measure the world precisely and are measured by it in return.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A quiet, meticulous man receives an anonymous commission to find the missing survey team, and against fifteen years of instinct, accepts. He travels into the monsoon-soaked interior and finds the camp intact but empty—boots, instruments, and a strange brass compass left behind. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine, the first crack in his carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Petra and Odile's POV alternating. Odile agrees to ferry him upriver for pay she badly needs, and they discover the surveyors' trail ends at a drowned village where the compass needle spins toward living people instead of north. Government boats begin sweeping the river. Emotional beat: wary partnership hardening into trust as both realize they're being hunted.

chapters.title: Needle and Noose
chapters.summary: Petra's POV with Odile interludes. Cornered in a flooded rail tunnel, they learn the sponsors want the compass destroyed and everyone who saw it silenced—and that the missing surveyors were taken alive. Petra realizes his own erased past made him the perfect deniable investigator. Climax: a night escape down rapids in the leaking boat, choosing each other over safety. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce loyalty.

chapters.title: True North
chapters.summary: Odile's POV closing on Petra. The sponsors' agent offers Petra restoration of his old name and career if he hands over the compass; instead he lets the river take it and exposes the survey records via Odile's river-network of smugglers and pilots. The monsoon breaks; the crew takes him in without ceremony. Emotional beat: resolution—he stops measuring life in miles and finally belongs somewhere.
